messages:
tara: quick check — seeing 'stale vram mapping' warnings in CI during async-offload -> host path. Nightly repro (small batch) and one prod trace. anyone seen this recently?

sam: which test / logs? can you paste the snippet or a repro script?

tara: pasted minimal log below from the host-fallback test run:
```
[evict] 0x7f3a2d: unbind_vram page_id=0x12af resident=true
[mmu] notifier: unmap queued for pfn=0x1a3
[race] access: kvcache_read hit while page->mapping==stale
[err] stale-vram-mapping: user saw stale mapping after unbind
```
Repro steps: run tests/fallback/host_fallback_test.sh --repeat 50 on a GPU node with async-offload=1

miguel: this smells like an ordering race between unbind and mmu notifier quiesce. possible window: evict path releases evict_lock right after unbind but before mmu notifier delivered to guest, so kvcache consumer can still see old mapping until notifier handler runs.

miguel: proposed invariant: "unbind_vram must not complete until mmu notifier confirms page unmapped for all contexts." Implementation idea (sketch):
```
acquire(evict_lock);
if (!page->resident) goto done;
page->state = EVICTING;
unbind_vram(page); // issue unmap / dma unbind
release(evict_lock);
wait_for_mmu_quiesce(page); // block until notifier callbacks processed
complete_evict(page);
```
This avoids transient visibility but adds latency on eviction path.

anya: can we instead barrier the kvcache path? e.g., check a page->mapping_epoch or a mapping_valid flag on read and if stale, fallback to remap/sync. cheaper on hot reads but still leaves writer complexity. Also we should add a unit test that injects mmu callback delays.

sam: +1 to mapping_epoch check. quick fix could be at kvcache_read: if (page->mapping_epoch != page->last_seen_epoch) goto slowpath; // slowpath waits/reads fresh mapping

I can prototype the epoch approach this week.

anya: for tests, suggest adding fault injection in CI: set MMU_DELAY=100ms in the notifier stub and run host-fallback N times to catch flakes. also add an assert that kvcache never returns mapping when mapping_valid==false.

offload-bot: CI: test/host-fallback (runner: gpu-32g-7) failed 3 times in last 24h — flake category: memory-ordering-race. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/12345

tara: thanks. I like the epoch check + test harness approach as a short-term mitigation. Miguel, can you sketch perf cost of waiting in eviction? if it's large we prefer epoch/bailout.

miguel: rough numbers: average eviction path latency + wait_for_mmu_quiesce ~ +1.2ms (measured on dev box with notifier loop). worst-case if delayed by GC-like stalls could be higher. So prefer epoch barrier to avoid adding latency to common evict path.

sam: ok i'll prototype epoch check in kvcache_read and add a small test that flips notifier delays. if that reduces flakes we can follow up with an RFC for a stronger ordering guarantee.

tara: i'll write an RFC follow-up checklist: 1) short-term epoch guard + tests, 2) perf run to measure kvcache slowpath cost, 3) long-term invariant change proposal (mmu quiesce in evict), 4) migration plan and rollback.

anya: also consider a telemetry counter for stale-mapping-drops so we can alert if epoch bailouts spike in prod.

sam: filed a PR draft: DRAFT: kvcache-epoch-guard. I'll link once CI passes.

tara: great. tagging @miguel @anya for review. I'll file the follow-up RFC with the checklist later today. :thumbsup:
